title: Invitation to Tender - Communities of Practice Development
description: CONTEXT Nature Towns and Cities is a UK-wide mission to bring nature and green space to urban areas for everyone's benefit. It is backed by coalition of public, private and third sector organisations committed to putting accessible nature at the heart of vibrant, healthy, resilient places and communities, focusing on those areas that will benefit the most. Over the next 10 years we're aiming to help 5 million more people enjoy better access to green and blue space close to home, and 1 million more children to be able to play in nature on their doorstep. THIS COMMISSION To support places and communities on their journey we have already provided training, peer mentoring, action learning, case studies and how to guides, conferences and events and informal opportunities to collaborate, though the Nature Towns and Cities Network. We now wish to develop and establish a small number of Communities of Practice to connect people and organisations working to create, improve and care for urban nature across the UK. These spaces will connect local government and wider public sector, national NGOs, VCSE organisations and possibly private sector organisations around shared ambitions for greener, fairer, healthier towns and cities. Communities of Practice is a working concept, intended to start coalescing the large Nature Towns and Cities network around purposeful activity on specific themes. We want to create spaces where network members can work through live challenges, share experience, learn from different perspectives and identify practical next steps. This commission will determine what these spaces look and feel like, and how they are delivered. INFORMATION TO BE RETURNED Tender responses should be sent to david.coughlin@nationaltrust.org.uk by the deadline of 12pm (midday) on 18/09/26 and include details of the following: • Outline of your proposed approach, including outputs • Description of your relevant experience, including examples of at least two pieces of similar work you have carried out. • Project timeline or Gantt chart • Key responsibilities of team members and time allocations • Proposed budget breakdown The budget available for this work is £50,000 inc VAT. title: Request For Proposal (RFP) for Pharmacological testing of novel opioids, stimulants, and synthetic cannabinoids.
description: Request For Proposal (RFP) for Pharmacological testing of novel opioids, stimulants, and synthetic cannabinoids. Amendment 1 - Questions & Answers #1 and Amendment to Annex B - SOW Stream 2 Amendment 2 - Questions & Answers #2 and Amendment to Annex A - SOW Stream 1 Novel psychoactive substances (NPS) in the illegal drug supply pose risks to Canadians. However, little is known about their pharmacological activity. More potent drugs increase the risk of overdose risks. Evidence on the pharmacological activity of these substances is essential to support scientific regulatory activities and risk assessments. The illegal drug supply is continuously evolving, with new substances continually being detected. There is a need for further information on their harms to Canadians. This procurement activity will allow for the evaluation of the in vitro pharmacological activity of three categories of emerging drugs: novel synthetic opioids, synthetic cannabinoids, and stimulants. The data generated from this contract will inform future assessment activities and allow the Office of Legislative and Regulatory Affairs (OLRA) to make more informed regulatory science decisions. For all three streams, they require the pharmacological testing of different classes of substances, and require acquisition of reference standards and control samples, getting licenses for controlled substances, conducting experiments (including doing statistical analysis), and finally drafting and finalizing reports. Canada is seeking offers from Offerors to provide Pharmacological Testing for Novel Opioids, Stimulants, and Synthetic Cannabinoids in three (3) separate streams to Health Canada. Stream 1 - In vitro pharmacological testing of emerging opioids at the Mu Opioid Receptor (MOR). Stream 2 – In vitro pharmacological testing of novel synthetic cannabinoids and Stream 3 – In vitro pharmacological testing of stimulant compounds. Each stream will be evaluated separately, and bidders are to provide their submissions for one (1) stream, two (2) streams or all three (3) streams. Up to three (3) contracts may be awarded under this request for proposal.

corrective actions throughout the lease period. m)Training materials and attendance records for operational and maintenance personnel, where required under Annex C. n)Record documentation showing final installed enclosure alignment, tie-ins, pass-through locations, movement corridor details, ESS device locations, infrastructure routes, equipment inventory, and associated record information. Sole Source Justification: The sole source determination is based on NOAA�s Sole Source Justification. Only one source is capable of providing the supplies or services required at the level of quality required because the supplies or services ordered are unique or highly specialized. ProSensing Inc. is the sole source capable of performing hardware-level modifications and specialized temperature- dependent calibration for the SFMR-HA due to their proprietary hardware ownership and specialized testing facilities. No other vendor possesses the requisite equipment or proprietary technical data to deliver validated operational calibration constants within the required timelines. Operational readiness of the SFMR-HA on the high-altitude aircraft (G-IV/G-550) is critical to NOAA's hurricane surveillance and atmospheric sampling missions.
